Ferroalloys Sectional Committee MTD 5 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 19 January 1990, after the 
draft finalized by the Ferroalloys Sectional Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical 
Engineering Divisional Council. 

Ferroaluminium is used for better control of de-oxidation during the making of semi-killed and killed 
steels. It is also used for alloy additions for iron and steel making. 

In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from UNE 35-083-85 'Ferroaluminium' 
published by the Institute Espanol de Normalizacion ( SPAIN ). 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the 
final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in 
accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revisedy. The number of signifi- 
cant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this 
standard* 



IS 12908 : 1990 



Indian Standard 
FERRO ALUMINIUM — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This Standard covers the requirements of 
ferroaluminium used in ferrous industry. 

2 REFERENCES 

2.1 The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard: 

IS No, Title 

1387:1967 General requirements for the 

supply of metallurgical materials 
(first revision ) 

1472 : 1977 Methods of sampling ferroalloys 

for determination of chemical 
composition (first revision ) 

1820 : 1979 Recommended shapes, sizes and 

mass of aluminium notched 
bars and ingots for remelting 
purposes (first revision ) 

3 TERMINOLOGY 

3.0 For the purpose of this standard, the follow- 
ing definitions shall apply. 

3.1 Cast ( Melt ) 

The product of any of the following: 

a) One furnace heat, or 

b) One tap of continuous furnace, or 

c) A number of furnace or crucible heats of 
similar composition mixed in a ladle or 
holding furnace and used for making a 
cast. 

3.2 Constitution of Consignment 
3.2.1 Tapped Lot Method 

A consignment constituted by the tapped lot 



method consists of a ferroaluminium mass of one 
melt ( or one part of a continuous tap ). 

3.2.2 Graded Lot Method 

A consignment constituted by the graded lot 
method consists of a number of melts ( or parts of 
continuous taps ) of one ferroaluminium designa- 
tion. 

The ferroaluminium content of the melts ( or 
parts of continuous taps ) constituting the 
consignment shall not differ from each other by 
more than 3 percent. 

3.2 J Blended Lot Method 

A consignment constituted by the blended lot 
method consists of a number of melts ( or parts 
of continuous taps ) of one ferroaluminium desi- 
gnation which have been crushed to a particle 
size less than 50 mm and thoroughly mixed. 

The content of the main constituent of the melts 
( or parts of continuous taps ) constituting the 
consignment may vary between the minimum and 
maximum limits specified for the appropriate 
ferroaluminium designation. 

3.3 Ferroaluminium 

A master alloy of iron and aluminium with a 
minimum aluminium content of 35*0 percent by 
mass and a maximum aluminium content of 50*0 
percent by mass obtained by fusion.

4.1 This standard covers two grades of ferro- 
aluminium as per the designation given in

5 CLASS 

5.1 Depending on the size of the granules and 
ingots, ferroaluminium has been classified in four 
classes as given in Table 2. 

6 PARTICULARS TO BE SPECIFIED WHILE 
ORDERING 

d.l For the benefit of the purchaser, particulars 
to be specified while ordering for the material to 
this specification shall be as follows: 

a) Quantity of the material; 

b) Constitution of consignment; 

c) Name of the material; 

d) Grade designation; 

e) Size range; 

f) Necessary requirements for analysis reports, 
packing, etc, as appropriate; and 

g) Shelf life. 

7 SUPPLY OF MATERIALS 

7.1 General requirements relating to supply of 
the material to this specification shall be as laid 
down in IS 1387: 1967. 

8 REQUIREMENTS 

8.1 Constitution of Consignment 

Ferroaluminium shall be delivered in consignments 
constituted by one of the methods defined in 3.2. 

8.2 Chemical Composition 

8.2.1 Each batch of the material shall conform to 
the requirements of the chemical composition 
specified in Table 1 and if so specified by the 
purchaser at the time of enquiry and order, shall 
supply a test certificate of chemical analysis of the 
sample of material for each melt, 

8.2.2 If specified by the purchaser at the time 
of enquiry and order that each lump of the batch 
should conform to the chemical composition 
specified in Table 1, this shall be agreed to 
between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 

NOTE — The material belonging to a melt which is 
out of specification, shall not be blended or mixed 
with the material of another melt. 

8.2.3 The chemical composition given in Table 1 
shows only the main constituents elements and 
usual impurities. If the purchaser requires closer 
ranges for the main element contents and/or 
different limits for specified elements and/or non- 
specified elements, this shall be agreed to between 
the purchaser and the manufacturer. 

8.2.4 The chemical composition of the material 



shall be determined by any established instru- 
mental/chemical method. Incase of dispute, the 
referee method shall be agreed to between the 
purchaser and the manufacturer till an Indian 
Standard is published. 

9 SIZE 

9.1 Unless otherwise specified, the material shall 
be supplied in lumps or as crushed and screened 
particles. The particle size ranges and tolerances 
shall be as given in Table 2. The undersize values 
shall be valid at the point of delivery to the 
purchaser.

of 250 mm 


ingot shall be 



10 DENSITY 

10.1 The density of the material shall be in the 
range of 5.5 to 6.1 g/cc. 

11 EXTRANEOUS CONTAMINATIONS 

11.1 The material shall be reasonably free from 
extraneous contaminations, namely, slag and 
non-metallic inclusions, etc. 

12 SAMPLING 

12.1 Each batch of the material shall be sampled 
in accordance with IS 1472 : 1977. 

13 PACKING 

13.1 The material shall be packed in suitable 
containers, in quantities as mutually agreed to 
between the supplier and the purchaser. 

14 MARKING 

14.1 The container shall be marked with the 
following: 

a) Supplier's name or trade-mark; 

b) Grade number and class; 

c) Quantity; 

d) Date of manufacture; and 

e) Shelf life, if required. 






Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the 
producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity 
to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
